method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Association of Urology (EAU) 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)' (limited update March 2026), 23 claims; LICENCE: © European Association of Urology 2026; personal and educational use only, no reproduction without written permission (read at section 7 'Copyright and terms of use' of the PDF itself). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76) 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction' (published online 7 February 2019), 12 claims; LICENCE: © 2019 Canadian Urological Association or its licensors; no reproduction without the prior written permission of the CUA (read at PMC6570608 JATS <permissions> element and the cuaj.ca article page copyright notice). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. The guideline's terms also state (verbatim): 'the EAU prohibits the usage or upload of its Guidelines, and any material derived from these texts (whether in full or in part) on external websites, bots, pages, portals, servers, software or external applications, including those employing artificial intelligence technologies and infrastructure, such as large language models and generative AI, deep learning and machine learning, unless written permission has been granted for such by the EAU.' Recorded per the standing owner decision (Wave 4); the content is paraphrased and hash-anchored. Edition 2.0 keeps every S1 claim unchanged and adds S2, the Canadian Urological Association guideline (2019, © CUA, paraphrased), read from its single-column online-first PDF (cua-a) because the two-column final PDF (cua-b) does not extract as running text; its risk-stratified surveillance figure (Figure 3) and tables were not machine-read.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Autonomic dysreflexia is an emergency to recognise:** it usually occurs with spinal cord lesions at or above T6 and is defined by a rise in systolic pressure of more than 20 mmHg over baseline, typically with severe headache, blurred vision and flushing and sweating above the lesion. A full bladder or bowel or an indwelling catheter can set it off, and it can be fatal if poorly managed.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnose and treat early,** in both congenital and acquired neurological disease, to stop permanent damage to the urinary tract.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a history of all four functions (bladder, bowel, sexual and neurological)** and look for alarm features such as pain, infection, haematuria or fever that need their own work-up. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline and routine tests:** urinalysis, blood chemistry, a bladder diary, post-void residual, a measure of leakage, and imaging of the urinary tract. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urodynamics is the only objective test of lower urinary tract function.** Do non-invasive tests first; for invasive studies use video-urodynamics, or if unavailable a filling cystometry that continues into a pressure-flow study. Monitor blood pressure and heart rate in anyone at risk of autonomic dysreflexia. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The kidneys are at risk, especially when the bladder fills at high pressure.** Spinal cord injury and spina bifida carry more risk of renal failure than slowly progressive conditions such as MS or Parkinson's disease. With low muscle mass, a cystatin C-based GFR detects kidney disease better than a creatinine-based estimate.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Everyone referred needs a urinalysis and a post-void residual at the first assessment (Grade B).** After spinal cord injury, the first urological review should happen within 6 months, earlier if there are worries (Grade A).
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Spinal cord injury, spina bifida and advanced MS need baseline urodynamics, a renal ultrasound and renal function tests (Grade A);** other causes have them when referred with a specific urological problem. Then class each patient as high, moderate or low risk to guide first treatment and surveillance (Grade B).
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hydronephrosis or reflux caused by high bladder pressure is treated by lowering storage pressure first;** anti-reflux surgery or ureteric stenting should not be used for it.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Priorities, in order: protect the upper tracts, achieve continence, restore lower tract function, and improve quality of life.** Holding bladder pressure within safe limits during filling and voiding is the top priority, because it cuts deaths from urological causes.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When the bladder is overactive or poorly compliant, the aim is a low-pressure reservoir,** even if that leaves residual urine.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discourage Credé (suprapubic pressure) and Valsalva straining** unless urodynamics shows bladder pressure stays safe: the pressures are harmful to the urinary tract, and these methods can worsen stress incontinence.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Triggered reflex voiding can also generate high pressure and can provoke autonomic dysreflexia in high spinal injuries,** so patients need training and close urodynamic follow-up.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never use a penile clamp with detrusor overactivity or low compliance:** it raises bladder pressure and risks pressure necrosis where sensation is reduced.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For neurogenic overactive bladder, use an antimuscarinic or a beta-3 agonist;** antimuscarinics are first-line for detrusor overactivity. Do not choose a beta-3 agonist to lower urodynamically proven overactivity, which it does not improve. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For poor emptying caused by outlet resistance, prescribe an α-blocker** (examples given: tamsulosin, naftopidil, silodosin); these lower outlet resistance, residual volume and autonomic dysreflexia. (Strong) See the banner on phenoxybenzamine, the PBS drug.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not use parasympathomimetics (such as bethanechol) for an underactive detrusor.** (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral antimuscarinics, with the dose pushed up as tolerated, are the first-line drug (Grade A);** evidence covers oxybutynin, tolterodine, propiverine, darifenacin and solifenacin. Combining two may help when dose escalation fails, and they are worth giving even with catheter drainage, because going without them is a risk factor for upper tract damage.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Intermittent catheterisation, by the patient or a carer, is the preferred method** when a neurological patient cannot empty the bladder. Sterile technique is not routine, and people need careful counselling before they start.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical practice: catheterise four to six times a day with a 12–16 Fr catheter, keeping each drained volume to no more than 400–500 mL.** Hydrophilic catheters are linked with fewer UTIs.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid indwelling urethral and, to a lesser degree, suprapubic catheters where possible,** because of complications and infection. If one is needed, prefer silicone (less encrustation, and latex allergy is common in this group); intermittent clamping brings no benefit. Investigate standard bladder-cancer red flags promptly in long-term catheter users.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Decide between intermittent and indwelling catheters with the patient,** and teach the technique and its risks thoroughly. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Match the drainage method to the person's motor function, anatomy, bladder behaviour, past complications and quality of life (Grade A),** and keep revisiting it. Self-catheterisation works best with a low-pressure bladder holding at least 350-400 mL, an unobstructed urethra and good hand function; strictures still occur in 4–13%.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Catheter care:** keep a closed drainage system closed, the bag below the bladder, and use pre-connected systems where possible. Indwelling catheters are usually changed every 2 to 4 weeks (monthly is commonest), though this is not evidence-based. Do not routinely use antibiotic- or silver-coated catheters, antiseptics in the bag or routine saline irrigation.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If antimuscarinics fail, inject botulinum toxin A into the detrusor** to reduce neurogenic overactivity. (Strong) The effect wears off after about nine months and repeat injections keep working.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urinary retention is a common adverse effect, so intermittent catheterisation may become necessary,** particularly in MS, where patients often do not catheterise beforehand; a 100 U dose may lower that need in MS.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CUA dose: onabotulinumtoxinA 200 units into the detrusor** for spinal cord injury or MS when an anticholinergic has not worked or is not tolerated (Grade A). 300 units works no better and makes catheterisation more likely; for abobotulinumtoxinA the best dose is 750 units (Grade B).
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not screen with urine dipsticks, and neither look for nor treat bacteriuria without symptoms,** in neurological patients. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For recurrent UTIs, first improve bladder management and remove foreign bodies such as stones or indwelling catheters.** Avoid continuous long-term antibiotics; weekly cycling of antibiotic prophylaxis can be offered to selected spinal cord injury patients who self-catheterise. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Call it a UTI only when leukocyturia, bacteriuria and symptoms are all present (Grade A).** Symptoms can be unusual: fever, new leakage, more spasticity, malaise, cloudy or smelly urine, back or bladder pain, dysuria, or autonomic dysreflexia.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Send a urine culture before any antibiotic (Grade A);** a catheter in place over 2 weeks should be replaced and the sample taken from the new one. Use narrow-spectrum drugs guided by local resistance, for 7 days when the response is prompt and 10–14 days for severe infection or a slow response (Grade A).
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **How the bladder is emptied is the main driver of UTI:** use clean intermittent catheterisation where possible (Grade A). A urethral indwelling catheter carries a more than 5-fold risk of recurrent UTI compared with suprapubic or intermittent catheterisation; suprapubic catheters bring more bladder stones.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Most patients should not have routine oral antibiotic prophylaxis (Grade A):** a meta-analysis of 15 RCTs found no support and about twice the resistance. Evidence is too thin for cranberry, probiotics, methenamine, D-mannose and similar measures; daily gentamicin bladder irrigation cut symptomatic UTI by 75% in people catheterising intermittently with recurrent UTI.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Follow up for life, tailored to risk:** in high-risk patients check the upper tracts and repeat urodynamics at regular intervals, and investigate any significant clinical change with a specialist. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CUA surveillance (Grade C, consensus):** see every patient yearly (rehabilitation physician, neurologist or GP), with a urologist involved at moderate or high risk, such as spinal cord injury, spina bifida or advanced MS. Renal and bladder ultrasound yearly at moderate or high risk; urodynamics yearly at high risk and every 2-5 years at moderate risk. No routine surveillance cystoscopy for bladder cancer, even after augmentation; use it for suspected urethral or bladder problems.
claims.locator: Kavanagh A, Baverstock R, Campeau L, Carlson K, Cox A, Hickling D, Nadeau G, Stothers L, Welk B (Canadian Urological Association), Can Urol Assoc J (doi 10.5489/cuaj.5912; final version 2019;13(6):E157-76), 'Canadian Urological Association guideline for the diagnosis, management, and surveillance of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction', published online 7 February 2019, https://cuaj.ca/index.php/journal/article/view/5912, retrieved 2026-09-24
